title: Give the agent a job and a receipt
learning_outcome: Define one bounded job and the receipt that would make its work reviewable.
exercise: Describe a familiar workflow; mark its owner, inputs, output, and first receipt.

boundaries.evidence: Use a synthetic workflow; omit actual prompts, identities, and private work traces.
boundaries.privacy: synthetic Harbor only; no actual participant, client, admin, or private corpus content
boundaries.authority: prepare_only; no live agent, memory promotion, message, booking, spending, or publication

scenes.narration_exact: “Friday afternoon. Morgan runs a small community learning program. For this course, we’ll follow Harbor Learning Circle, an illustrative case built from fictional records. Someone suggests adding a free digital-skills session next month. Three notes are on the table: an attendance count, a facilitator availability note, and a room-capacity note. An assistant can turn those into a neat recommendation in seconds. But if Morgan asks, ‘Where did this come from?’ a polished paragraph is thin protection. The work needs a trail.”

scenes.narration_exact: “Our job today is small: design one preparation role and one receipt. The agent does not decide whether the session happens. It prepares a Session Option Brief for Morgan to review. That distinction matters. If we give the system a loose command like ‘run the workshop program,’ we have no useful boundary. What exactly begins its work? What can it read? What must it hand back? Who owns the outcome? These are ordinary management questions. They become more urgent when a tool can produce work while nobody is watching.”

scenes.narration_exact: “Write the job in one sentence: ‘When Morgan requests a monthly session review, prepare one brief comparing a proposed free session against the three cleared inputs.’ The trigger is Morgan's request. The output is a draft brief. The manager is Morgan. The measure is whether Morgan can check the claim and source for every recommendation without chasing the agent through a log. The forbidden actions are just as plain: no booking, no announcement, no message to participants, no spending. A useful agent job names the work it finishes and the work it leaves alone.”

scenes.narration_exact: “Now attach the receipt. Imagine the brief says the room can hold twenty people. Morgan needs to see which note supplied that number, when the brief was prepared, what the agent actually did, and whether anyone approved it. The receipt also records cost or resource use, outcome, and how to pull the draft back. A blank field stays blank and gets an owner. We never fill a gap with a confident guess. The first receipt is a handoff a busy person can understand; the engineering log can remain behind it.”
scenes.on_screen_copy_exact: “Receipt: intent • agent • source • action • artifact • approval • cost • outcome • rollback.”

scenes.narration_exact: “In our case, approval is ‘pending Morgan.’ The outcome is ‘draft prepared, no session selected.’ The rollback is ‘withdraw the draft from the review folder and mark it superseded.’ If the source for room capacity is missing, mark the brief blocked. A complete-looking card without a source can move bad information faster than an obviously unfinished one. The receipt makes that gap visible before anyone treats the draft as a decision.”

scenes.narration_exact: “Fill the Job and Receipt boxes. Name the trigger, permitted inputs, output, human manager, success check, and three forbidden actions. Then fill the nine receipt fields for one imaginary run. If you cannot name a source, approval state, or rollback, write ‘unknown’ and the person who must resolve it. Do not open a real system to complete this exercise. The point is to see the shape of the work before asking a tool to do it.”
